scope: synthetic defensive Qubes/qrexec worker readiness only

winner.approach: deterministic report evaluator over measured VM-boundary campaign outputs
why: keeps the existing qrexec protocol semantics unchanged
separates environment execution from readiness policy
fails closed on malformed or insufficient evidence
gates both correctness invariants and latency budgets
adds negligible runtime/resource overhead and low regression risk
is replayable in CI from captured synthetic campaign reports

alternatives.approach: hard-code Qubes command execution directly into the Node test suite
alternatives.rejectedBecause: couples correctness tests to Qubes availability and produces noisy CI

alternatives.approach: manual operator review of raw qrexec logs
alternatives.latency: low implementation cost but high review cost
alternatives.rejectedBecause: cannot provide a deterministic readiness decision

alternatives.approach: deterministic report evaluator over measured VM-boundary campaign outputs
alternatives.correctness: high when the campaign collector is trustworthy

lessons: A green process-boundary test is not evidence of a green VM-boundary test.
Readiness must be derived from captured evidence, not inferred from transport similarity.
Correctness counters are release blockers even when latency is excellent.
Insufficient sample size must fail closed rather than silently classify the worker as ready.
